nodes.characterization_summary: SEM cross-section and top-view images show no delamination or structural change of Raney-Ni coating after 15 min ultrasonication in 30 wt.-% KOH at 25°C, confirming coating stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen in Figure 4 that ultrasound does not influence the stability of the Raney-Ni coating and the cross-section shows no delamination of the Raney-Ni under ultrasonic conditions.

properties.description: Porous material with irregular granular morphology, clusters of particles ~1-5 μm, rough surface texture

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Raney-Ni determined from CV in non-faradaic region: 0.37 mC at 25°C, 1.31 mC at 40°C, 3.28 mC at 60°C. Electrochemical surface area (Aecsa) calculated as 9.25 cm², 32.82 cm², 82.00 cm² respectively using specific capacitance density of 40 μF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical surface area (Aecsa) was determined electrochemically by calculating the double-layer capacitance, Cdl, from cyclic voltammetry (CV) experiments... Table 1 Double-layer capacitance (Cdl), electrochemical surface area (Aecsa) and specific surface area (As) of Raney-Ni at various temperatures.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at E = -200 mV vs RHE for HER: charge transfer resistance Rct decreases from 11.59 Ω (silent) to 6.31 Ω (US) at 25°C, 2.01 Ω to 1.67 Ω at 40°C, 0.49 Ω to 0.47 Ω at 60°C. Capacitance C increases with temperature and US at lower temperatures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 10 shows the Nyquist representation of the impedance data... The parameters obtained from the EIS measurement are shown in Table 4.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at E = +1550 mV vs RHE for OER: charge transfer resistance Rct changes from 2.015 Ω (silent) to 1.494 Ω (US) at 25°C, 0.97 Ω to 1.27 Ω at 40°C, 0.50 Ω to 0.64 Ω at 60°C. Capacitance values reported in Table 5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 11 shows the Nyquist representation... The values for each circuit element/parameter are given in Table 5.
